headline: Severe gas crisis grips Dhaka: CNG stations face long queues, supply disruptions
summary: Drivers and transport sector workers are in distress due to the severe gas shortage, with many stations closing or experiencing low pressure.
details: Dhaka is currently grappling with a severe and ongoing gas crisis, leading to extensive queues at CNG filling stations. Drivers are forced to wait for hours to receive minimal gas, while many stations have ceased operations entirely due to low pressure or halted supply.

The situation has particularly impacted low and middle-income drivers, including those operating CNG-powered auto-rickshaws and ride-sharing services. Many report significant drops in daily income as they are unable to transport passengers without adequate fuel.

The crisis intensified after gas supply from Accelerate Energy's LNG terminal was completely shut down on Wednesday, August 19, at 3 PM. This disruption was caused by an insufficient supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in the pipeline.

The prolonged shortage continues to cause widespread inconvenience for city dwellers and the transport sector. Efforts to resolve the persistent fuel scarcity have been slow, exacerbating the challenges faced by commuters and businesses.

headline: Bangladesh holds presidential election today after 35 years, with 349 MPs to vote
summary: The nation's 23rd president will be elected by 349 Members of Parliament, marking only the second time MPs have voted for president since the reintroduction of the parliamentary system in 1991.
details: Bangladesh is holding its presidential election today, August 20, marking the first time in nearly 35 years that a vote will take place. The voting process will run from 2 PM to 5 PM in the Jatiya Sangsad (National Parliament) chamber.

A total of 349 Members of Parliament (MPs) will elect the country's 23rd president. The candidates facing off in this election are Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir from BNP and Oli Ahmad from the 11-party alliance.
Three transparent ballot boxes will be set up in the Parliament chamber for the voting. MPs will cast their ballots using a designated method and deposit them into the boxes.

Following the conclusion of voting, the ballots will be counted within the Parliament chamber. The results will then be announced by the electoral officer and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) A M M Nasir Uddin.

The Election Commission (EC) is expected to publish a gazette notification today itself. The newly elected president is scheduled to take the oath of office on Friday evening, August 21, at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.
This election is only the second time MPs will vote for president since the reintroduction of the parliamentary government system in 1991. The previous seven presidents were elected unopposed.

The Election Commission (EC) is expected to publish a gazette notification today itself. The newly elected president is scheduled to take the oath of office on Friday evening, August 21, at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.
